method: Read current main workbook before testing the prior trace; distinguish direct/particular religious content, specific complementary support and unestablished religious application. These descriptive categories impose no count or quota.

courses.name: Personal & Professional Development
courses.previousTrace: Mandatory first-year academic and personal formation.
courses.sourceFirstJudgment: Academic writing, source criticism and reflection are retained as verified skills. PPD is a required course, not evidence that a religion-centred programme has been established.
courses.selectionDisposition: Preserved in review history; withdrawn from active counselor comparison. This is not a finding that the course is intrinsically unsuitable.

courses.name: Law, Society & Justice
courses.previousTrace: Teaches legal systems, justice and law/society relations; provides the formal foundation for comparative constitutional study.
courses.sourceFirstJudgment: Legal systems, law/society and justice can support analysis of religious communities, but the documented course does not require such analysis. Its prerequisite role is mechanically valid; that does not establish target comparability.
courses.selectionDisposition: Preserved in review history; withdrawn from active counselor comparison. This is not a finding that the course is intrinsically unsuitable.

courses.name: Human Rights: Law & Philosophy
courses.previousTrace: Studies Aquinas, natural law, rights and historical/philosophical justifications, contributing concrete value-and-authority inquiry.
courses.roleInTargetAssessment: Specific related content and legal support
courses.sourceFirstJudgment: Aquinas, natural law and rights in traditional societies are concrete relevant content. Their role within a broad rights course does not supply sustained study of religious claims or communities.
courses.selectionDisposition: Preserved in review history; withdrawn from active counselor comparison. This is not a finding that the course is intrinsically unsuitable.

courses.name: Comparative Constitutional Law
courses.previousTrace: Examines constitutional values, state institutions and religious constitutions through a comparative legal approach; no theology curriculum is inferred.
courses.sourceFirstJudgment: description2 includes religious constitutions; the profile covers comparative constitutional/administrative law. This supports a limited religion/state perspective, not comparative religious traditions or the interpretation of their beliefs. The earlier trace is not treated as fabricated, but its target-level weight was overstated.
courses.selectionDisposition: Preserved in review history; withdrawn from active counselor comparison. This is not a finding that the course is intrinsically unsuitable.

courses.name: Introduction to Western Philosophy
courses.previousTrace: Examines knowledge, the existence of god, meaning, responsibility and philosophical argument.
courses.sourceFirstJudgment: Existence of God, meaning, Western philosophical history and argument genuinely contribute. The World Philosophy relationship is retained as a real partial correspondence, without implying full global or religion-philosophy coverage.
courses.selectionDisposition: Preserved in review history; withdrawn from active counselor comparison. This is not a finding that the course is intrinsically unsuitable.

courses.name: Ethics
courses.previousTrace: Supplies explicit moral theories and applied ethical reasoning; not comparative religious ethics.
courses.sourceFirstJudgment: Moral theories and applied ethics are concrete complementary tools. The evidence does not establish religious ethics, theological traditions or comparison of religious truth claims; moral reasoning alone cannot carry that inference.
courses.selectionDisposition: Preserved in review history; withdrawn from active counselor comparison. This is not a finding that the course is intrinsically unsuitable.

courses.name: Philosophy of Mind
courses.previousTrace: Examines self and personal identity, including Buddhist thought, alongside mind and consciousness.
courses.sourceFirstJudgment: Buddhist theories of self occur explicitly within a broader consciousness/mind course. This is a genuine connection, not a sustained Buddhist or comparative-religion sequence.
courses.selectionDisposition: Preserved in review history; withdrawn from active counselor comparison. This is not a finding that the course is intrinsically unsuitable.

courses.name: Philosophy of Emotion
courses.previousTrace: Examines the nature and rationality of emotion and its relation to ethics and art; contributes philosophical inquiry into affect and value, not psychology of religion.
courses.sourceFirstJudgment: Emotion, ethics, rationality, politics and art make a coherent contribution to the new philosophy concept. No documented religious object, tradition or required religious inquiry connects its substantial place in this programme to the target.
courses.selectionDisposition: Preserved in review history; withdrawn from active counselor comparison. This is not a finding that the course is intrinsically unsuitable.

courses.name: Free Will, Time & the Self
courses.previousTrace: Studies freedom, luck, time and the self as substantive philosophical questions of agency and responsibility.
courses.sourceFirstJudgment: Free will, time, luck and self are legitimate philosophical questions. The source does not establish theological treatment, religious experience or systematic comparative-worldview inquiry. Their possible relevance is insufficient as the target bridge.
courses.selectionDisposition: Preserved in review history; withdrawn from active counselor comparison. This is not a finding that the course is intrinsically unsuitable.

courses.name: Introduction to Political Philosophy
courses.previousTrace: Examines authority, freedom, equality, pluralism and multiculturalism as frameworks for shared public life.
courses.sourceFirstJudgment: Authority and political institutions can support religion/public-life questions, but the actual course does not require those questions. General political philosophy cannot be counted as their implementation.
courses.selectionDisposition: Preserved in review history; withdrawn from active counselor comparison. This is not a finding that the course is intrinsically unsuitable.

courses.name: Peace & Conflict
courses.previousTrace: Studies ideological conflict, grievances, reconciliation and conflict transformation as a defined public-life context, without relabelling it religious conflict.
courses.sourceFirstJudgment: Ideological conflict, reconciliation and historical grievance can support a defined religious-conflict inquiry. The evidence does not establish that this programme teaches interreligious conflict/dialogue; earlier not-substantively-distinct rejection relied on the now-withdrawn public-life strand.
courses.selectionDisposition: Preserved in review history; withdrawn from active counselor comparison. This is not a finding that the course is intrinsically unsuitable.

courses.name: Introduction to Sociology
courses.previousTrace: Supplies sociological theories of institutions, social relations, race, class and gender for the belief-and-public-life strand.
courses.sourceFirstJudgment: Social institutions and classical sociological theory are useful foundations. The record does not demonstrate a taught sociology-of-religion investigation, and naming general institutions does not establish it.
courses.selectionDisposition: Preserved in review history; withdrawn from active counselor comparison. This is not a finding that the course is intrinsically unsuitable.

courses.name: Qualitative Research Methodology
courses.previousTrace: Teaches qualitative design, collection and interpretation of empirical social data; supplies an actual research method.
courses.sourceFirstJudgment: Qualitative design, data collection, reflexivity and interpretation can materially support religious inquiry. Student choice of topic is not a guaranteed religion-focused project or supervised disciplinary sequence; no such required application is encoded.
courses.selectionDisposition: Preserved in review history; withdrawn from active counselor comparison. This is not a finding that the course is intrinsically unsuitable.

courses.name: Modern Sociology
courses.previousTrace: Studies modernity, imperialism and colonial responses as substantive contexts of social and cultural meaning.
courses.sourceFirstJudgment: Modernity, imperialism and colonial responses can contextualise religious change. The supplied profile does not establish an inquiry into religious change; that application cannot simply be assumed.
courses.selectionDisposition: Preserved in review history; withdrawn from active counselor comparison. This is not a finding that the course is intrinsically unsuitable.

courses.name: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory
courses.previousTrace: Studies civil society, solidarity, the public sphere and empirical inquiry with civic organisations; not sociology of religion as a specialist course.
courses.sourceFirstJudgment: Civil society, solidarity and empirical work with NGOs are concrete teaching, but the programme does not specify religious organisations or a religious-studies method. It cannot treat generic civic inquiry as coverage of religion in society.
courses.selectionDisposition: Preserved in review history; withdrawn from active counselor comparison. This is not a finding that the course is intrinsically unsuitable.

courses.name: Social Psychology
courses.previousTrace: Studies social influences on thoughts, beliefs and behaviour; supports a specific social account of belief without claiming psychology of religion.
courses.sourceFirstJudgment: Social influence on thoughts/feelings/behaviour is relevant to belief in a broad sense. The source does not establish religious belief, religious experience or religious coping; the earlier interest ownership silently broadened religious belief to belief generally.
courses.selectionDisposition: Preserved in review history; withdrawn from active counselor comparison. This is not a finding that the course is intrinsically unsuitable.

courses.name: Introduction to World Archaeology
courses.previousTrace: Examines material production in relation to religious, social and gendered identities across ancient societies.
courses.sourceFirstJudgment: Craft and material production are explicitly related to religious, social and gendered identities across ancient societies. This is substantive relevant material, while the course remains organised around archaeology and making rather than comparison of religious practices.
courses.selectionDisposition: Preserved in review history; withdrawn from active counselor comparison. This is not a finding that the course is intrinsically unsuitable.

courses.name: African Art & Heritage
courses.previousTrace: Studies religious, cultural and social meaning in western-African visual traditions and the ethics of collection and repatriation.
courses.sourceFirstJudgment: Western-African visual traditions explicitly embody religious meaning. Collection/repatriation ethics and global artistic influence are also important course content. This is a valuable bounded religious-cultural contribution, not a general survey of religious traditions.
courses.selectionDisposition: Preserved in review history; withdrawn from active counselor comparison. This is not a finding that the course is intrinsically unsuitable.

courses.name: Renaissance Italy & Global Mediterranean
courses.previousTrace: Studies Renaissance art through cross-cultural exchange, including Islamic courts; contributes a defined artistic context rather than Islamic theology.
courses.sourceFirstJudgment: The description includes Islamic courts within Renaissance artistic exchange. It documents an artistic context, not Islamic belief, religious interpretation or spiritual practice. No enriched profile is available; only documented description scope is used.
courses.selectionDisposition: Preserved in review history; withdrawn from active counselor comparison. This is not a finding that the course is intrinsically unsuitable.

courses.name: Heritage & Ancient Democracy
courses.previousTrace: Examines Athenian democracy intertwined with myth and religion, its material expression and political participation.
courses.sourceFirstJudgment: The profile explicitly connects Athenian democracy, myth and religion through material heritage and simulation. It is a strong concrete case contribution, but its organising subject is ancient democracy rather than sustained comparative religious inquiry.
courses.selectionDisposition: Preserved in review history; withdrawn from active counselor comparison. This is not a finding that the course is intrinsically unsuitable.

courses.name: Introduction to Literary Studies
courses.previousTrace: Teaches interpretation of literary forms and narratives, providing tools for the text-and-meaning strand.
courses.sourceFirstJudgment: Practical criticism and literary genres provide real analytical tools. No required sacred-text material, theological hermeneutic or religious interpretive practice is documented; those tools do not by themselves supply the target subject.
courses.selectionDisposition: Preserved in review history; withdrawn from active counselor comparison. This is not a finding that the course is intrinsically unsuitable.

courses.name: Great Literary Works
courses.previousTrace: Studies literary representations of organised religion, duty, freedom and community within a wider literary history.
courses.sourceFirstJudgment: Organised religion is explicitly one of several themes in a broad literary survey. This supports a bounded contribution, without turning the whole course into scripture, Christian history or comparative religion.
courses.selectionDisposition: Preserved in review history; withdrawn from active counselor comparison. This is not a finding that the course is intrinsically unsuitable.

courses.name: World Myth & Literature
courses.previousTrace: Directly compares mythic narratives across ancient, Indian, Byzantine and Arabic traditions, text and image.
courses.sourceFirstJudgment: Cross-cultural myth, literary transmission, oral/visual forms and comparison are directly relevant. Retain the partial VU myth correspondence; VU also teaches ritual and the disciplinary debate in myth/ritual studies, so equivalence is not claimed.
courses.selectionDisposition: Preserved in review history; withdrawn from active counselor comparison. This is not a finding that the course is intrinsically unsuitable.

courses.name: Perspectives on Literary Meaning
courses.previousTrace: Teaches humanist, feminist, Marxist, cultural-minority and psychoanalytic interpretations and a text-based research project.
courses.sourceFirstJudgment: Humanist, feminist, Marxist, cultural-minority and psychoanalytic readings plus a text project supply real methods. The evidence does not establish sacred-text interpretation or dialogue across religious traditions. A possible religious text choice is not a required programme component.
courses.selectionDisposition: Preserved in review history; withdrawn from active counselor comparison. This is not a finding that the course is intrinsically unsuitable.
